content:
hey everyone i'm having a great time learning lean4 and working through the examples in mathematics_in_lean as well as other real analysis examples.

one thing i'm really having a tough time with is learning when to apply linarith, nlinarith, congr, gcongr, norm_num, field_simp, ring, ring_nf.

for me sometimes that's the most frustrating part. for example, sometimes i'll be stuck on a problem for half an hour, and then realize it's because i couldn't apply gcongr because i didn't put epsilon / 2 in brackets.

do you think people eventually get used to it, and eventually develop an instinct for when to use what? or is it one of those problems that are like, okay, just feed it to claude and get claude to see where you failed? how do you recommend going about getting better at spotting which tactic to use?

wishing everyone a happy monday!

I just fallback to calc proofs in this case. I know how Lean works so I don't have to rely on fancy automation.

But grind is quite useful I must say.
There are a very small number of tactics so yes it gets better when you know what they do, and reading their docstrings is hopefully a useful way to learn.
